ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Guided MoE Routing by Task-Conditioned Experts
PROPOSAL: We will design and train a MoE model with a novel routing mechanism that uses task-conditioned routing weights. Each expert is associated with a specific task or sub-task, and the routing weights are conditioned on the input's task labels. This design allows the model to generate route assignments that are optimized for the specific task requirements, rather than just load balancing. We will evaluate this design on various language modeling benchmarks and compare its performance to a standard MoE model with uniform routing.
CONTROLS: We will use a standard MoE model as a baseline, and ablate the task-conditioned routing mechanism to see if it has an impact on expert routing and specialization.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours (estimated time to train 5 language model checkpoints with and without task-conditioned routing)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on language modeling tasks that are optimized for task-conditioned routing, with a potential 5-10% increase in perplexity. However, the improvement may be limited by the difficulty of accurately labeling tasks and the risk of over-specialization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Regularized Routing by Expert Orthogonality
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the effect of regularizing the routing weights to encourage orthogonality among experts. By applying a orthogonality regularizer to the routing weights, we aim to prevent experts from developing overly similar or redundant representations, which can lead to expert homogenization. We will evaluate the impact of this regularizer on expert routing patterns and specialization, as well as its effect on downstream performance on various language modeling and knowledge question-answering tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the regularized model to a standard MoE model, and ablate the regularizer to see if the results are due to the orthogonality promotion or other effects.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours (estimated time to train 3 language model checkpoints with and without the regularizer)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on downstream tasks, with a potential 2-5% increase in accuracy. However, the regularizer may have a detrimental effect on expert routing patterns if not carefully tuned, leading to reduced performance on certain tasks.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE:  Regularized Routing by Expert Orthogonality
PROPOSAL: (revision) We will use a novel orthogonality regularizer that encourages each pair of experts to have minimal overlap in their output distributions. This regularizer will be applied to the probability-weighted average of the output distributions of each pair of experts. We will also explore the effect of the regularizer's strength and the number of experts on the convergence of the MoE model.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the regularized model to a standard MoE model and investigate the effect of the regularizer's strength and number of experts on the results.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours (estimated time to train 3 language model checkpoints with varying regularizer strength and number of experts)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on downstream tasks and more diverse expert output distributions, which may lead to better knowledge representation and reasoning capabilities. However, the regularizer may require careful tuning to balance its benefits and potential detrimental effects on model convergence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Domain-Specific Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of domain-specific knowledge distillation to guide the development of expert models in a MoE architecture. Specifically, we will train a small teacher network on a large dataset in each domain and use its output to supervise the training of the corresponding expert models. This should encourage the experts to develop more specialized and accurate representations for each domain.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the expert models distilled from a teacher network to those trained from scratch, and investigate the effect of the teacher network's learning rate and batch size on the results.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours (estimated time to train 4 teacher networks and their corresponding expert models)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on tasks that require domain-specific knowledge, with a potential 5-10% increase in accuracy. However, the method may require careful tuning of the teacher network's parameters to avoid over-supervision and degraded expert performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Routing Spectrum Analysis
PROPOSAL: We will develop a framework to analyze and visualize the routing spectrum of a MoE model, which captures the distribution of routing probabilities and expert activations across the model's input space. This will allow us to study the properties of expert specialization and routing diversity in more detail, and identify potential issues such as expert homogenization.
CONTROLS: We will compare the routing spectra of MoE models trained with different routing mechanisms, including task-conditioned experts and domain-specific knowledge distillation.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (estimated time to train a few MoE models and analyze their routing spectra)
PREDICTION: We expect to gain insights into the relationship between expert specialization and routing diversity, and identify conditions under which expert homogenization is more or less likely to occur. However, the analysis may require careful engineering to extract meaningful insights from the routing spectrum.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Contrastive Expert Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will develop a contrastive expert regularization method to encourage the development of more diverse and specialized expert models in a MoE architecture. Specifically, we will use a contrastive loss function to separate the output distributions of each pair of expert models, and encourage them to learn more distinct representations.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the MoE model trained with contrastive expert regularizer to that of a standard MoE model and a MoE model with regularized routing.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours (estimated time to train 5 MoE models with varying degrees of contrastive regularization)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on downstream tasks and more diverse expert output distributions, which may lead to better knowledge representation and reasoning capabilities. However, the method may require careful tuning of the regularization strength and hyperparameters to obtain optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Expert Shareability Analysis
PROPOSAL: We will develop a framework to analyze the shareability of expert models across different downstream tasks. This will involve identifying and ranking the experts according to their level of shareability, and studying the characteristics of the experts that are most and least shareable.
CONTROLS: We will use a set of diverse downstream tasks to evaluate the shareability of the expert models trained with different routing mechanisms and regularization methods.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours (estimated time to train a few MoE models and perform shareability analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect to gain insights into the relationship between expert shareability and the routing mechanisms used, and identify conditions under which expert shareability is more or less likely to occur. However, the analysis may require careful engineering to extract meaningful insights from the expert shareability metric.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Meta-Learning for Expert Transfer
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of meta-learning to enable the transfer of expertise across different tasks and domains. Specifically, we will train a meta-learner that can adapt to new tasks and domains using the expert models trained with different routing mechanisms and regularization methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the meta-learner trained with experts from different routing mechanisms and regularization methods, and evaluate its ability to adapt to new tasks and domains.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours (estimated time to train a meta-learner and evaluate its performance on a set of downstream tasks)
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance on new tasks and domains, and a more efficient adaptation process. However, the method may require careful tuning of the meta-learner's hyperparameters and the expert models' architectures to obtain optimal results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Large-Scale Ensemble MoE Evaluation
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a large-scale evaluation of the MoE models trained with different routing mechanisms and regularization methods. Specifically, we will train a diverse set of MoE models on a variety of language modeling tasks and evaluate their performance on a range of downstream tasks, including math reasoning and reading comprehension.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the MoE models trained with different routing mechanisms and regularization methods, and evaluate the transferability of their expertise to new tasks and domains.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours (estimated time to train a large set of MoE models and evaluate their performance on a range of downstream tasks)
PREDICTION: We expect to see a more comprehensive understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of MoE models trained with different routing mechanisms and regularization methods, and identify conditions under which each method is most effective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Routing with Conditional Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: Implement a Conditional MoE architecture, where the routing policy (indices of active experts) depends on soft attention weights output by a secondary neural network. The routing network will take the latent representation of the input sequence as input, allowing the MoE to selectively choose experts that are relevant to specific input subspaces, thereby guiding the specialization of experts.
CONTROLS: Compare to the standard MoE routing policy, and an ablation study of replacing the routing network with a simpler learnable inspector heuristic.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Reduces expert homogenization and leads to improved specialization, yielding better performance on downstream tasks in both English and Chinese language modeling, while preserving the efficiency benefits of the original MoE.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Supervised Routing with Input-Relevant Expert Attributes
PROPOSAL: Introduce a supervisory signal to train the routing policy to select experts based on input-relevant attributes, such as parts-of-speech tags, named entity recognition, or dependency parse trees, which are either annotated and available during pre-training or can be estimated using a secondary autoencoder model. This signal incentivizes the experts to develop specialized representations that directly correspond to the input's structural properties.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on the vanilla MoE without supervised routing and compare to the performance of the Conditional MoE from proposal 1.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Exhibits better performance than vanilla MoE and Conditional MoE in tasks such as exam-style knowledge question answering and reading comprehension, particularly when input attributes are strongly relevant to the task, and may further assist downstream tasks by enriching the representation of input content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble Heterogeneity Promoting Objective (EHP)
PROPOSAL: Introduce an auxiliary loss function to optimize the heterogeneity of the ensemble, encouraging the MoE to learn a diverse set of experts with minimal overlap in their input spaces. EHP can be achieved by penalizing the maximum overlap of the input regions assigned to each expert or by promoting a measure of structural heterogeneity between experts, such as differences in their weight parameters or Latent space representation distributions.
CONTROLS: Compare EHP against standard MoE and other aires of the previous proposals (e.g., propose ablations where experts are fixed while routing diversity is enhanced).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Combines well with the techniques from proposals 1 and 2, leading to significantly improved downstream performance in both English and Chinese language modeling benchmarks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Routing with Shared Experts
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical routing mechanism, where a coarse-level expert selector chooses a subset of experts to consider at a high level, and then a fine-level expert selector further narrows down the choices within that subset. Shared experts across different levels can be used to capture common functionalities, such as syntax or domain knowledge, allowing the model to specialize in more specific tasks while still benefiting from general knowledge.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on the vanilla MoE and compare to other proposals, also including an ablation study that removes shared experts and relies on separate experts for each task.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrates improved task-specific performance and flexibility, allowing the model to tackle more diverse and complex tasks, while maintaining the efficiency benefits of the MoE architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Knowledge Distillation for Expert Training
PROPOSAL: Implement an adversarial knowledge distillation (AKD) mechanism to encourage experts to develop complementary knowledge representations. The AKD process involves a teacher expert and a student expert that are trained to disagree on a subset of tasks, promoting the student expert to learn novel representations. This leads to a more diverse ensemble of experts and improved performance on downstream tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional knowledge distillation and to a subset of the other proposals, with an ablation study that trains the experts independently without AKD.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Significantly boosts the performance of the MoE model by encouraging experts to develop distinct knowledge representations, resulting in improved zero-shot and few-shot adaptation to new tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Expert Initialization
PROPOSAL: Use meta-learning to initialize the experts, where a meta-model is trained to learn the parameters of an expert initialization function. The meta-model takes in a task description or a set of input samples and outputs a set of expert initialization parameters. This enables the model to adapt quickly to new tasks and learn specialized representations for each task.
CONTROLS: Compare to random initialization and to the other proposals, with an ablation study that fixes the expert initialization parameters across tasks.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrates improved adaptability and knowledge transfer across tasks, enabling the MoE model to learn specialized representations for each task more efficiently.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Expert Merging for Dynamic Task Streams
PROPOSAL: Introduce an online expert merging mechanism, where experts that are highly similar or redundant are merged into a single expert. This enables the model to adapt to dynamic task streams and learn specialized representations for each task quickly, reducing the risk of over-specialization and improving overall performance.
CONTROLS: Compare to a static expert setting and to a subset of the other proposals, with an ablation study that removes the expert merging mechanism.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Enhances the model's ability to adapt to changing task requirements and dynamic input streams, leading to improved performance and reduced computational overhead in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for MoE Models
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the quality of MoE models, including metrics for expert diversity, knowledge representation, and task adaptation. This framework will enable a systematic comparison of the proposed techniques and provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each approach.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed techniques using a range of tasks and datasets, including language modeling, question answering, and reading comprehension.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Provides a quantitative and qualitative understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each proposed technique, enabling researchers to make informed choices about the most effective approaches for their specific use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Expert Routing through Conditional Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: We propose a new conditional routing loss that modulates the standard load-balancing loss with a learned prior preference over expert distributions. This learned prior forces each expert to develop a distinct specialization by maximizing a token-level diversity metric, such as normalized entropy, across the batch. By incorporating this metric into the load-balancing loss, we structure the routing scheme to favor dissimilar expert selection patterns across tokens and encourage organized collaboration. The conditional routing loss will be formulated as $L_{cond} = L_{loadbalancing} + \lambda H(\pi_x)$, where $\lambda$ is a hyperparameter, $H(\pi_x)$ is the normalized entropy of expert distributions across tokens $x$, and $\pi_x$ denotes the probability distribution over experts for token $x$. We will explore the choice of $\lambda$ and its impact on expert specialization and model performance in the experiments.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method to standard teacher forcing with and without the global load-balancing loss, as well as modifications that punish expert homogenization through various regularizers.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed conditional routing loss will lead to improved expert specialization, fewer redundancies, and enhanced model performance in language modeling tasks, particularly on non-densely distributed datasets. Where it might fail is in excessively over-specializing experts, leading to fragmented representations that compromise the global modeling capabilities. To mitigate this, we may need to adjust the value of $\lambda$ or incorporate an additional regularization term to maintain sufficient overlap across experts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-enriched Expert Routing for Identifying Coherent Expert Specializations
PROPOSAL: To further refine expert specializations, we propose a novel context-enriched expert routing mechanism that incorporates token-level contextual information into the routing decision. Specifically, we will augment the MoE architecture with an attention mechanism that selectively aggregates contextual information from a fixed-size window around each token to facilitate more informed expert selections. This approach can help overcome the limitations of the conditional routing loss by allowing experts to build upon contextual relationships across tokens. By integrating the context-aware expert routing module with the proposed conditional routing loss, we aim to foster more coherent and adaptable expert specializations.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the performance of this approach by comparing it to the scenario where only contextual information is utilized for routing, as well as the original conditional routing loss without context incorporation.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed context-enriched expert routing module will enhance expert specializations by taking into account the intra-sentence dependencies and relationships between tokens, leading to a more nuanced and adaptive model performance. However, its success may also depend on the quality and scope of the contextual information used, which could introduce new challenges in expert over-specialization and computational cost. To address these concerns, we may need to experiment with various context window sizes and attention mechanisms.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Context-enriched Expert Routing for Identifying Coherent Expert Specializations
PROPOSAL: To further refine expert specializations, we revise the context-enriched expert routing mechanism to incorporate not only token-level contextual information but also the learned distributed representations of the embedded tokens. This can be achieved by modifying the context aggregation mechanism to incorporate the embedded token representations and expert gating, allowing experts to selectively attend to relevant contextual information for informed expert selections. This revised approach will enable experts to develop more contextualized and cohesive specializations, which can lead to enhanced model performance in recognizing underlying patterns within the input data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the revised context-enriched expert routing mechanism to the original approach with contextual information and without context incorporation, as well as to a baseline where no contextual information is used.
COST: 25 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised context-enriched expert routing mechanism will improve expert specializations by incorporating the learned token embeddings and expert gating, leading to more nuanced and adaptive model performance. However, this revised approach may also increase the complexity of the MoE architecture and require additional training data, which could potentially impact its real-world applicability and deployment in resource-constrained settings.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Guided Expert Routing through Conditional Routing Loss
PROPOSAL: We refine the conditional routing loss by incorporating an entropic regularization term to the prior distribution over expert specializations, which encourages the learned prior to be more diffuse and varied. This can be formulated as $L_{cond} = L_{loadbalancing} + \lambda H(\pi_x) - \alpha H(\pi)$, where $\alpha$ is a hyperparameter controlling the strength of the regularization and $H(\pi)$ is the entropy of the prior distribution itself. The entropic regularization term can help mitigate the risk of the prior distribution converging to overly specialized and redundant expert specializations.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the revised conditional routing loss with entropic regularization to the original approach, as well as to modifications that punish expert homogenization through various regularizers.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The entropic regularization will lead to a more diverse and adaptive prior distribution over expert specializations, which will improve model performance in capturing complex relationships within the input data but may also increase the risk of over-fitting and decreased robustness to noise and outliers. To mitigate this, we may need to tune the value of $\alpha$ or experiment with alternative regularization schemes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical MoE for Identifying Domain-Specific Expert Specializations
PROPOSAL: To tackle the challenge of identifying domain-specific expert specializations, we propose a hierarchical MoE architecture where a dense subset of experts serves as a "domain expert" that guides the routing process for the remaining experts. Specifically, we will use a set of domain-dedicated experts to condition the routing probability distribution of other experts, allowing the model to capture domain-specific behavior and knowledge. By organizing experts into a hierarchical structure, we can enable the model to learn diverse and specialized representations for different domains.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the hierarchical MoE approach to the original MoE architecture with and without the conditional routing loss, as well as to a baseline where the domain expert routing mechanism is replaced with a simpler global load-balancing loss.
COST: 35 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hierarchical MoE architecture will allow the model to capture domain-specific behavior and improve expert specialization, leading to enhanced model performance in tasks that require adapting to different domains. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality of the domain-dedicated experts and the ability of the model to effectively learn from the domain-specific guidance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterative Self-Modification of Expert Routers for Adaptive Specialization
PROPOSAL: To further adapt the expert routers to changing data distributions and improve specialization, we propose an iterative self-modification mechanism where the model modifies its own routing probabilities through a learned process. Specifically, we will add a secondary neural network that takes the outputs of the expert routers as input and outputs a set of parameters that modify the routing probabilities. This secondary network will be trained jointly with the MoE model to adapt to changing data distributions and improve expert specialization. By allowing the model to iteratively modify its own behavior, we can enable the MoE architecture to adapt to a wide range of tasks and data distributions.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the iterative self-modification mechanism to the original MoE architecture with and without the conditional routing loss, as well as to a baseline where the secondary network is replaced with a fixed set of rules.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The iterative self-modification mechanism will enable the MoE architecture to adapt to changing data distributions and improve expert specialization, leading to enhanced model performance in real-world applications. However, the success of this approach may depend on the stability of the training process and the ability of the secondary network to generalize to new tasks and data distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Expert Specialization through Transfer Learning and Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the quality of expert specialization in the MoE architecture, we propose a transfer learning and domain adaptation setup where we fine-tune the pre-trained MoE model on a new task or domain and measure the extent to which the expert specializations adapt to the new task or domain. We will compare the performance of the MoE model in adapting to the new task or domain to a baseline where the expert specializations are randomly initialized or frozen during fine-tuning. This will provide insights into the ability of the MoE model to generalize expert specializations across multiple tasks and domains.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the MoE model in the transfer learning and domain adaptation evaluation to a baseline where the expert specializations are randomly initialized or frozen during fine-tuning.
COST: 25 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The evaluation of expert specialization through transfer learning and domain adaptation will provide insights into the generalization of MoE models across tasks and domains. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality of the pre-trained MoE model and the difficulty of the new task or domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert Discovery through Unsupervised Clustering and Merging
PROPOSAL: To identify the most specialized and effective experts in the MoE architecture, we propose an unsupervised clustering and merging approach where we group experts based on their similarity in routing probabilities and merge clusters of experts that specialize in similar tasks or subtasks. We will use a hierarchical agglomerative clustering algorithm to identify clusters of experts and a clustering validation metric to evaluate the quality of the clusters. By identifying the most specialized and effective experts, we can improve the overall performance of the MoE model and reduce computational costs.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the expert discovery approach to a baseline where all experts are treated equally.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The expert discovery through unsupervised clustering and merging will help identify the most specialized and effective experts in the MoE architecture, leading to improved performance and reduced computational costs. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality of the clustering algorithm and the choice of validation metric.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding Expert Interactions through Multi-Task Learning and Evaluation Metrics
PROPOSAL: To better understand the interactions between experts in the MoE architecture, we propose a multi-task learning setup where we train the MoE model on multiple task-specific datasets and evaluate the performance of individual experts across tasks. We will use a combination of task-specific evaluation metrics and a shared evaluation metric to evaluate the performance of individual experts and identify potential areas for improvement. By understanding the interactions between experts, we can identify opportunities to improve the MoE architecture and develop more effective training protocols.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the multi-task learning setup to a baseline where the MoE model is trained on a single task.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The understanding of expert interactions through multi-task learning and evaluation metrics will provide insights into the performance of individual experts and identify potential areas for improvement. However, the success of this approach may depend on the choice of evaluation metrics and the quality of the task-specific datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Efficient MoE Training through Parallelization and Pruning
PROPOSAL: To improve the scalability and efficiency of MoE training, we propose a parallelization and pruning approach where we train the MoE model in parallel across multiple GPUs and prune redundant experts during training. We will use a combination of model parallelization and data parallelization to train the MoE model, and a pruning algorithm to remove redundant experts. By parallelizing the training process and pruning redundant experts, we can improve the training time and computational efficiency of the MoE model.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the parallelization and pruning approach to a baseline where the MoE model is trained sequentially without pruning.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The scalable and efficient MoE training through parallelization and pruning will significantly improve the training time and computational efficiency of the MoE model, making it more suitable for large-scale applications. However, the success of this approach may depend on the quality of the pruning algorithm and the choice of model and data parallelization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structured Routing Through Orthogonal Expert Attachments
PROPOSAL: This experiment builds upon recent works that use regularizers to promote orthogonality of the router's weight matrix. We propose adding a regularizer that encourages attachments of experts to form an Hadamard basis of the input representation, thereby structuring the routing diversity into meaningful expert attachments. Specifically, we test this regularizer in conjunction with a batch-level load balancing loss, where the routing diversity term is computed over the entire batch, rather than per micro-batch. This design guides the experts to develop attachments that complement each other in a structured way.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the standard training paradigm with load balancing loss and to the baseline where the router's weights are randomly initialized and no regularizer is used, to assess the impact of our designed constraint on expert attachments.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By structuring the routing diversity, our approach is expected to alleviate expert homogenization, leading to more diverse experts with both improved language modeling and downstream performance in tasks such as mathematical reasoning and reading comprehension.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Routing Loss for Representational Specialization
PROPOSAL: To further encourage representational specialization among experts, we propose introducing a multi-task routing loss. Specifically, we modify the batch-level load balancing loss to encourage the router to develop diverse attachments for different tasks within a single input sequence, resulting in adaptive routing schemes for diverse tasks on a single sequence. We then fine-tune the expert attachments on a single-task objective while maintaining the multi-task routing loss, allowing the experts to develop a task-specific expertise.
CONTROLS: We compare this approach to the standard training paradigm with a load-balancing loss and no task-specialization guidance. We also compare it to our previous experiment, Structured Routing Through Orthogonal Expert Attachments, to evaluate the combined benefit of orthogonal attachments and task-specialized routing.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed multi-task routing loss is expected to lead to expert attachments that not only reduce homogenization but also improve across-task and across-token performance, allowing the model to adapt to diverse tasks within a single sequence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-Student Routing for Improved Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: This experiment focuses on reducing expert homogenization by incorporating a teacher-student routing mechanism. In this setup, a 'teacher' MoE is pre-trained on the entire dataset, and its routing scheme is used to guide the training of a 'student' MoE that starts with randomly initialized weights. We leverage the idea that the teacher's routing scheme contains information about how to divide the representation across experts, while the student learns to replicate this routing scheme for improved representational specialization.
CONTROLS: We compare this method to our previous approaches, Structured Routing Through Orthogonal Expert Attachments and Multi-Task Routing Loss for Representational Specialization, by combining them with the teacher-student routing. We also compare to a student-only training approach to evaluate the benefit of teacher guidance.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging pre-existing knowledge from a teacher model, the student MoE is expected to develop more diverse expert attachments with better downstream performance in tasks such as mathematical reasoning and reading comprehension, likely mitigating expert homogenization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning Routing Adamants
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we introduce a meta-learning approach for learning task-agnostic routing adamant-like modules that promote diverse expert attachments across tasks.
